input: Write a cover letter for a grant application

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The nature of the project or cause being funded completely shapes the content, language, and evidence needed in the letter.
Whether the applicant is an individual, nonprofit, academic institution, or business changes the tone, credentials to highlight, and how to frame the request.
The specific grant body and its mission determine what values, priorities, and language to align with in the letter.
Deadlines and word or page limits directly affect how much detail can be included and how urgently the draft is needed.
The desired tone — formal vs. personal, data-driven vs. story-led — determines how the letter is structured and written.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like (e.g., securing a specific amount, advancing to next review stage) helps frame the letter's call to action and key asks.
Whether the user needs a full draft, an outline, or a polished final version shapes how much work needs to be done and in what format to deliver it.

gold.taskTitle: Write a grant application cover letter
gold.taskDescription: Write a compelling cover letter to accompany a grant application for a specific funding opportunity.

questions.title: What project or cause is the grant funding?
questions.description: Understand the subject matter — research, community programme, arts project, etc. — so the letter's content is accurate and relevant.

questions.title: Who is the applicant — individual, organisation, or institution?
questions.description: Identify who is applying so the letter uses the right voice, credentials, and framing for the applicant type.

questions.title: Which specific grant body or funder is this addressed to?
questions.description: Know the funder's name, mission, and priorities so the letter can be tailored to their values and language.

questions.title: Is there a word limit or submission deadline to meet?
questions.description: Establish any hard constraints on length or timing that affect how the letter is scoped and how quickly it must be produced.

questions.title: What tone should the letter strike — formal, personal, data-driven?
questions.description: Determine the preferred writing style so the letter resonates with both the funder's culture and the applicant's voice.

questions.title: What funding amount is being requested, and for what outcome?
questions.description: Clarify the specific ask and the measurable result it will achieve, which anchors the letter's call to action.

questions.title: Do you need a full draft, an outline, or a final polished letter?
questions.description: Confirm the desired deliverable format so the right level of effort and structure is applied from the start.
